full_judgment:
Shahabuddin Ahmed, C.J: In the Leave Petition No. 327 of 1991 defendant-petitioner No.1 is the wife of defendant-petitioner No. 2. Petitioner No.2 has appeared to argue the himself by our permission. H is challenging an order of a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division dated 9 July, 1991, in Civil Revision No.2286 of 1990. This revision application has been allowed and the rule issued thereon has been made absolute with a direction upon the trial tout to dispose of the petitioner's application under Section 151 Civil PC. "on merit". His contention is that instead of sending the matter to the trial Court the learned Single Judge should have himself decided it on merit by setting aside the impugned ex-part a decree which, according to him, is absolutely, totally and on the fact of the record itself, fraudulent and bad. By the same order of the learned Single Judge, the other party namely, plaintiff-petitioner in the Leave Petition No.331 of 1991 has also felt aggrieved and she has come here challenging the said order. She is respondent No. 1 in Leave Petition No. 327 of 1991, and will be referred to, here as the "respondent". 

 2. Respondent filed T.S. No.100 of 1974 in the Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge for specific performance of a contract for sale of a two storied building on a 13-katha land at 3, Baily Road, Dhaka against the petitioners, but lost it at all stages including the Appellate Division. Findings of the Courts below were that the alleged agreement for sale was "fraudulent and void". But on the strength of that agreement she had forcibly taken possession of the ground floor of the building. These findings were accepted by the Appellate Division in its judgment dated 18 March, 1986, in Civil Petition No. 113 of 1985, which was dismissed. About four months thereafter, the respondent filed another suit, T.S. No.183 of 1986, in the Fourth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka, for permanent injunction in respect of the self-same property and obtained an ex-parte decree on 14 July, 1987. The petitioners, alleging that this suit was filed concealing the real facts and the ex-parte decree was obtained by fraudulent suppression of summons, tiled before the trial court as application under Section 151 Civil P.C. for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground of "fraud practiced upon the Court". The trial Court rejected the application on the ground that the application under Section 101 C.P.C. is not maintainable in view of alternative remedies available including remedy under Order IX, Rule 13 C.P.C. The petitioners challenged this order before the High Court Division in the civil revision, as mentioned above, and prayed for setting aside the decree on the ground of fraud apparent on the face of the record including the judgment of the Appellate Division. The question raised before the learned Single Judge was: "Is the civil court so powerless that in exercise of its inherent powers it cannot entertain an application for setting aside an expert decree which is alleged to have been obtained on practicing fraud upon the Court itself?" After hearing both parties the learned Single Judge answered the question in the negative, held that the application under Section 151 C.P.C. is maintainable observed that the trial Court fell into an error by refusing to entertain the application and direct the trial Court to dispose of the application "on merit".
